Thresholds and SLOs must be calibrated on separate data, versioned, and changed only through recorded configuration. Do not infer platform-specific values without measurement.

Falsifiable hypothesis (verification-priority scheduling): enabling verification-priority scheduling with a bounded, fail-closed fallback will reduce speculative end-to-end p95 latency or increase decode throughput (tokens/s) versus the current speculative path, without worsening target-equivalent output quality, error rate, memory safety, or the declared SLO. Predeclare an improvement margin and guardrail limits; the hypothesis is falsified if the margin is missed or any guardrail fails.

Controlled experiment: randomly assign matched requests to target-only, current speculation, or current speculation plus the intervention, stratified by prompt length (tokens), generated length (tokens), arrival rate (requests/s), concurrency (requests), and workload class. Use warm-up, repeated trials, confidence intervals, and a held-out replay. Compare per-request and aggregate results at equal offered load, and report both absolute and relative effects.

Measure draft latency (ms/request and ms/token), target verification latency (ms/verification), end-to-end latency (ms/request; p50/p95/p99), throughput (tokens/s and requests/s), acceptance rate by speculative position (%), accepted tokens per speculation step (tokens/step), draft/target work (tokens/s), synchronization and queue-wait overhead (ms/request), retries/rollbacks (count/request), GPU/CPU utilization (%), memory and KV-cache high-water mark (MiB), and cost (currency/request if available). Record timestamps and configuration IDs so stages sum to end-to-end latency.

Interpretation and confounders: separate draft compute, target verification, rejection/recompute, synchronization, admission, and queueing; stratify by workload and inspect interactions rather than averaging them away. Check clock synchronization, warm-up, batching, compiler/cache state, thermals, background load, rate-limit behavior, sampling variance, retries, and measurement overhead. Compare output equivalence and quality with the same seeds/policy; do not treat acceptance alone as a speedup.

Boundaries and safety: cap speculative depth, batch size, queue delay, memory/KV use, retries, and CPU/GPU work. Disable the intervention and fall back to target-only or the known-good current path on timeout, invalid cache/tokenizer state, quality mismatch, error/SLO breach, resource pressure, telemetry loss, or unsafe dependency overlap. Canary gradually, retain raw traces and rollback logs, and stop on any prespecified hard limit. Evidence required before adoption is a reproducible randomized comparison, per-position and stage-level traces, held-out workload replay, target-equivalence/quality checks, uncertainty intervals, and an expert review; absent that evidence, keep the result provisional.
